Issues.Title: Keep COM test composition variable alive through end of scope.
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #


## Proposed changes

- Keep the `Composition` instance in `TryGetIStreamData_DoesNotDoubleReleaseStream` reachable through the final unmanaged refcount assertion.
- Add `GC.KeepAlive(composition)` at the intended liveness boundary; no production COM ownership or release logic changes.
- `GC.KeepAlive(obj)` intentionally tells the JIT/GC that `obj` remains reachable through the call. It does not read or modify the object, dispose it, allocate a `GCHandle`, permanently root it, extend its lifetime beyond the call, or force immediate collection/finalization afterward. Here it keeps `Composition`, its adapters, and their `AgileComPointer` fields reachable, preventing finalizers from revoking GIT entries and releasing two COM references before the assertion. Normal collection and finalization may occur after the call, so cleanup semantics are unchanged.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Removes a net481/x86 test flake caused by the JIT considering `composition` dead before the test's final native refcount probe.
- No product behavior changes.

## Regression? 

- No

## Risk

- Low. This is a test-only managed-lifetime boundary with no production code changes.

There are conflicting commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via automated merge. 
The situation is rare but normal. The target branch is expected to receive manual commits in the Azure DevOps clone, which could cause conflict.

Conflicts need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

- you can resolve the issue by resolving the conflict in the **target branch only**. 
    - Please make sure that the changes sensitive from security perspective are not published ahead of time to GitHub!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the conflict is resolved.

Issues.Title: Let each platform declare the TYMEDs it supports so WPF can provide enhanced metafiles
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/wpf#11986

Companion WPF PR: dotnet/wpf#11988

## Proposed changes

- Add `IOleServices.AllowedTymeds`, following the existing `#if NET static abstract` pattern.
- `Composition` reads the allowed media types from the platform instead of the hard-coded `TYMED_HGLOBAL | TYMED_ISTREAM | TYMED_GDI`, in both the managed-to-native and native-to-managed adapters.
- `WinFormsOleServices` returns the old value, so WinForms behavior is unchanged. WPF adds `TYMED_ENHMF` in the companion PR.

## Customer Impact

- On .NET 10, WPF apps can't provide `CF_ENHMETAFILE` to other applications: every `TYMED_ENHMF` request fails with `DV_E_TYMED` before WPF's handler runs. Pasting EMF into apps like Word fails silently, with no workaround.

## Regression?

- Yes. .NET 9 WPF allowed `TYMED_ENHMF`, and the shared mask dropped it.

## Risk

- Low. WinForms gets the same value as before, and `IOleServices` is internal.
- The value is per platform rather than added to the shared constant, because WinForms can't supply or read EMF. A shared value would make WinForms report EMF as available when it isn't.

## Test methodology

- Added `ManagedToNativeAdapterTests`, which fails with `DV_E_TYMED` without this change.
- `System.Private.Windows.Core.Tests` passes on net11.0 and net481.
- Validated end-to-end with a WPF app on .NET 11 RC 1, using WPF built with the companion change: EMF paste now works for delayed and flushed data.

## Test environment(s)

- .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103, Windows 11 (10.0.26200)

Issues.Title: DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown allow height changes in VisualStylesMode.Net11 instead of reverting to the original height
Issues.Body:
### .NET version

.NET 11 SDK build: 11.0.100-rtm.26477.103

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Not tested/verified

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

New APIs in .NET 11

### Issue description

When VisualStylesMode is set to Net11, the DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown controls allow their Height property to be changed through the Visual Studio Properties window.
This behavior is inconsistent with VisualStylesMode = Classic. In Classic mode, after entering a different Height value and pressing Enter, the value immediately reverts to the control's original height.
In Net11 mode, however, the new height is accepted and the control is resized in the Designer. After closing and reopening the Form Designer, the control returns to its original height.
The behavior in Net11 mode should be consistent with Classic mode and should not accept a height value that cannot be preserved.

VisualStylesMode: NET11

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1249b23-7ae8-41bf-b348-fc261088bf3c

VisualStylesMode: Classic

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c427e0ad-ab03-4a4e-a6b3-c2f3aa699b63


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a WinForms project and open a form in the Form Designer.
2. Set VisualStylesMode to Net11.
3. Add a DomainUpDown and a NumericUpDown control to the form.
4. Select each control and change its Height value through the Visual Studio Properties window.
5. Press Enter after entering the new height value.
6. Observe the height value and the controls in the Designer.
7. Close and reopen the Form Designer.

**Actual Result:**
With VisualStylesMode set to Net11, the new height value is accepted after pressing Enter. However, after closing and reopening the Form Designer, the DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown controls revert to their original heights.

**Expected Result:**
The behavior should be consistent with VisualStylesMode = Classic. When changing the Height value through the Properties window and pressing Enter, the value should immediately revert to the control's original valid height rather than accepting a height that cannot be preserved.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Fix FailFast crash in LabelEditNativeWindow due to garbage collected WinEvent hook delegate
Issues.Body:
Backport of #14663 to release/11.0

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/14657

## Description
Window destroyed → hooks not unregistered → object garbage collected → hook callback invokes freed memory → crash (`FailFast`).

The original code skipped cleanup when handle was gone, leaving orphaned hooks running.

## Fix
- Added `UnhookWinEventHooks()` method to centralize hook cleanup
- Call unhook when handle is destroyed in `OnHandleChange()`
- Added `_isReleasing` flag to prevent reentry during cleanup
- Set `_winEventProcCallback = null` after unhooking to allow GC

## Customer Impact
Applications using screen readers (e.g., Narrator) no longer crash when editing `PropertyGrid` or `TreeView` with accessibility enabled.

## Testing
- Manually

## Regression? 

- No

## Risk

- Minimal: only defensive guards added, no behavior changes.

Issues.Title: Raise UIA state change events for CheckBox and RadioButton
Issues.Body:
Fixes #15201

Related: #15176

## Proposed changes

- `CheckBox`: raise the `ToggleState` property-changed event, with the old and new values, whenever `CheckState` changes (checked, unchecked and indeterminate). It follows `ToolStripButtonAccessibleObject.OnCheckStateChanged`: `CheckBoxAccessibleObject` gets the same `OnCheckStateChanged(oldValue, newValue)` method, and `CheckBox` keeps the previous `CheckState` to pass it. The mapping from `CheckState` to `ToggleState` moves to a private helper shared by the `ToggleState` property and the new method.
- `RadioButton`: raise `ElementSelected` when the radio button is checked and `ElementRemovedFromSelection` when it is unchecked, including when another radio button of the group unchecks it. Only when the accessible object supports the SelectionItem pattern, so a custom accessible object that does not is left alone.
- Both controls no longer raise a `Name` property change with the same old and new value, nor `UIA_AutomationPropertyChangedEventId` as a plain automation event. They were a workaround so that clients would re-read the control, and the events above make them unnecessary. For `RadioButton` the `Name` change came from #5766, for #5235 (Narrator not reading radio buttons fully with the arrow keys); without it Narrator still reads them in full ("Small, radio button, checked").
- The state is taken before the MSAA notifications, which run synchronously.

## Customer Impact

- UIA clients now receive the state change events that the UI Automation specification requires for the CheckBox and RadioButton control types, as they did on .NET Framework. Narrator, for example, now announces just the new state when a check box is toggled, instead of re-reading the whole control because of the `Name` change.
- NVDA uses MSAA for these controls, so for NVDA the relevant fix is #15177.

## Regression?

- Yes, from .NET Framework and .NET Core 3.1. There these controls had no UIA provider of their own and UI Automation's MSAA proxy raised these events (measured on .NET Framework 4.8, see the issue). Since .NET 5 (#3228, #3244) WinForms serves its own UIA provider for them, and it does not raise them. The events raised now are the same ones, in the same order, with the old `ToggleState` value added.

## Risk

- Low. Only the UIA events change, in the same places that already raised the MSAA and UIA notifications: the state events are added and the `Name` change workaround is removed. Checked with Narrator, JAWS and NVDA (see below). No change to how the controls behave or look, and no public API change.

## Test methodology

- New unit tests in `CheckBoxTests`: the `ToggleState` change with its old and new values for every transition between the three states, no event when the same value is set again, the same with a window handle, and the event when the state is changed through the Toggle pattern. In `RadioButtonTests`: `ElementSelected` and `ElementRemovedFromSelection` when checking and unchecking, with and without a window handle, and `ElementRemovedFromSelection` on a sibling unchecked by the group. A `RadioButton` whose accessible object does not support SelectionItem raises no selection events. All of them fail without the change, except the two that check that no event is raised (the same value set again, and the custom accessible object).
- `CheckBox_RaiseAutomationEvent_Invoke_Success` and `RadioButton_RaiseAutomationEvent_Invoke_Success` count the events raised; their expected counts now match the new events.
- Ran the `CheckBox`, `RadioButton` and accessible object test classes for both controls (868 tests) after removing the `Name` change: all pass.
- Listened to the UIA and MSAA events of a small app from another process on .NET Framework 4.8, .NET 9, .NET 10 and .NET 10 with the change (logs in the issue).
- Manual testing on Windows 11 with a local build of `release/10.0`, with this change alone and together with #15177:
  - Narrator: before, a state change re-read the whole control (name and state); after, it says only the new state. Moving through radio buttons with the arrow keys still reads them in full ("Small, radio button, checked").
  - JAWS 2026 (2026.2608.25.400): no change; it keeps announcing every state change once, including those made by code while the control has the focus.
  - NVDA 2026.2.0: no change with this PR alone, as expected. Together with #15177 it announces every state change, including those made by code.

## Accessibility testing

Axe.Windows 2.4.2 (the engine of Accessibility Insights for Windows) run against the repro app attached to the issue, before (stock .NET 10.0.12) and after (the same app with this change), with the window idle and again after checking the check box, advancing the three-state check box and moving to the next radio button from the keyboard:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | 0 errors | 0 errors |
| After the state changes | 0 errors | 0 errors |

No new error. Axe.Windows checks the UIA tree and its properties, not events, so it does not see the missing events themselves; the events were checked with the event listener and the screen readers described above.

## Test environment(s)

- .NET SDK 10.0.303, runtime 10.0.12, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200.

Issues.Title: CheckBox and RadioButton do not raise the UIA events for their state changes (ToggleState, ElementSelected), unlike on .NET Framework
Issues.Body:
### .NET version

.NET 10 (10.0.12) and .NET 9 (9.0.20). Same code in `main`.

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Yes

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

.NET Core 3.1, going by the code (I measured .NET Framework 4.8, .NET 9 and .NET 10): there `CheckBox` and `RadioButton` had no UIA provider of their own, as on .NET Framework. It stopped in .NET 5, when #3228 and #3244 added their UIA providers.

### Issue description

When a `CheckBox` is checked or unchecked, or a `RadioButton` is checked, WinForms raises no UI Automation event that tells a client what changed. I am a blind developer, and I found it while looking into #15176.

The UI Automation specification lists these events as required:

- [CheckBox control type](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/winauto/uiauto-supportcheckboxcontroltype#required-ui-automation-events): the `ToggleState` property-changed event.
- [RadioButton control type](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/winauto/uiauto-supportradiobuttoncontroltype#required-ui-automation-events): `ElementSelected` and `ElementRemovedFromSelection`, when the control supports the SelectionItem pattern, as `RadioButtonAccessibleObject` does.

What `CheckBox.NotifyAccessibilityStateChanged` and `RadioButton.OnCheckedChanged` raise on the UIA side is:

```csharp
using var nameVariant = (VARIANT)Name;
AccessibilityObject.RaiseAutomationPropertyChangedEvent(UIA_PROPERTY_ID.UIA_NamePropertyId, nameVariant, nameVariant);
AccessibilityObject.RaiseAutomationEvent(UIA_EVENT_ID.UIA_AutomationPropertyChangedEventId);
```

That is a `Name` change whose old and new values are the same, and `UIA_AutomationPropertyChangedEventId` raised as a plain automation event. Neither says that the state changed. `ToolStripButton` already does it right: it raises the `ToggleState` change with its old and new values (`ToolStripButtonAccessibleObject.OnCheckStateChanged`).

On .NET Framework 4.8 and .NET Core 3.1 these controls had no UIA provider of their own, so UI Automation served them through its MSAA proxy, which turned their MSAA state change into exactly these events. Since .NET 5 (#3228, #3244) WinForms serves its own UIA provider for them, so the proxy is no longer involved, and that provider does not raise them. `RadioButton` raised an `IsSelected` property change in .NET 5 and 6 (with the old and new values swapped); #5766 replaced it with the `Name` change above to fix #5235, where Narrator did not read radio buttons fully when moving with the arrow keys.

Screen readers on Windows 11 today: Narrator (UIA only) and JAWS 2026 announce the change indirectly, re-reading the whole control when the `Name` change arrives. NVDA uses MSAA for these windows, so it depends on the MSAA state change instead (see #15176).

<details>
<summary>Measurements: the events seen from another process</summary>

The attached app, with the keys sent from another process: Space on the check box "Notifications", Space three times on the three-state check box "Sync mode", Down twice in the radio group, then the timed change while the focus is on the radio group. Only UIA events are shown. `Name` changes are left out, except in the .NET 10 block, where they are the only events.

.NET Framework 4.8 (4.8.9325.0). The MSAA proxy raises one `ToggleState` change for each MSAA state change, the pressed state included, so there are several per key press, and the old values are null because the proxy does not know them:

```
==== Space on the check box
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Notifications" old=null new=0
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Notifications" old=null new=1
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Notifications" old=null new=1
==== Down (radio group)
UIA  FocusChanged: RadioButton "Medium"
UIA  ElementRemovedFromSelectionEvent: "Small"
UIA  ElementSelectedEvent: "Medium"
==== timed change, focus on "Large"
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Notifications" old=null new=0
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Sync mode" old=null new=1
UIA  ElementRemovedFromSelectionEvent: "Large"
UIA  ElementSelectedEvent: "Small"
```

.NET 10.0.12 (the same on 9.0.20):

```
==== Space on the check box
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Notifications" old= new=
==== Space on the three-state box (1)
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Sync mode" old= new=
==== Down (radio group)
UIA  FocusChanged: RadioButton "Medium"
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Small" old= new=
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Medium" old= new=
==== timed change, focus on "Large"
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Notifications" old= new=
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Sync mode" old= new=
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Large" old= new=
UIA  PropertyChanged NameProperty: "Small" old= new=
```

.NET 10 with the change I am proposing:

```
==== Space on the check box
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Notifications" old=0 new=1
==== Space on the three-state box (1), (2), (3)
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Sync mode" old=0 new=1
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Sync mode" old=1 new=2
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Sync mode" old=2 new=0
==== Down (radio group)
UIA  FocusChanged: RadioButton "Medium"
UIA  ElementRemovedFromSelectionEvent: "Small"
UIA  ElementSelectedEvent: "Medium"
==== timed change, focus on "Large"
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Notifications" old=1 new=0
UIA  PropertyChanged ToggleStateProperty: "Sync mode" old=0 new=1
UIA  ElementRemovedFromSelectionEvent: "Large"
UIA  ElementSelectedEvent: "Small"
```

</details>

I have the change with unit tests ready and will open a pull request.

### Steps to reproduce

[WinFormsStateEventsRepro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32698064/WinFormsStateEventsRepro.zip)

The attached app (source only, `dotnet run`, targets .NET 10; its README says how to switch it to `net48` or `net9.0-windows` to compare) has a check box, a three-state check box, a radio group and a button that changes all the states by code 5 seconds later. Its README has the full steps. In short:

```csharp
CheckBox checkBox = new() { Text = "&Notifications", AutoSize = true };
Controls.Add(checkBox);
```

1. Listen to UIA property-changed events for `ToggleState` on the window, for example with Accessibility Insights for Windows (event mode) or the `AccEvent` tool of the Windows SDK.
2. Focus the check box and press Space.
3. No `ToggleState` change is raised; only a `Name` change with the same value.

The same with a `RadioButton` and the SelectionItem events: checking another radio button of a group raises neither `ElementSelected` nor `ElementRemovedFromSelection`.

Issues.Title: DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize can terminate the process with 0xc0000005 for an offline printer queue
Issues.Body:
> Disclosure: This issue report was prepared by OpenAI Codex, an AI coding agent, from diagnostic information and test results supplied by the application developer. The report should be reviewed by a human before submission. Customer-identifying information has intentionally been omitted.

### .NET version

- Target framework: `net10.0-windows`
- Process architecture: x64
- .NET runtime: `10.0.12`
- CoreCLR: `10.0.1226.42308`
- Application type: WPF application using `System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings`

### Description

Reading `PrinterSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize` for one or more offline printer queues can terminate the entire process with native exception code `0xc0000005`.

The failure cannot be caught by normal managed `try/catch`; the process terminates before error logging in the catch block can run.

The problem reproduces on a customer Windows system but not on the developer workstation or server. The application starts normally when printer detail reads are disabled. Isolating the queried properties showed:

- Printer enumeration succeeds.
- Reading `PrintQueue.IsOffline` succeeds.
- Reading `PrinterSettings.PrinterResolutions` succeeds.
- Reading `PrinterSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize` causes the native crash.
- Skipping printer detail reads when `PrintQueue.IsOffline == true` prevents the crash. The resulting build has been deployed to the customer and operates successfully.

This may ultimately be caused by a printer driver returning malformed `DEVMODE` data. Nevertheless, a public managed property getter terminating the process without a catchable managed exception is unexpected.

### Minimal code path

```csharp
using System.Drawing.Printing;
using System.Printing;

using var server = new LocalPrintServer();
var queues = server.GetPrintQueues(
    [EnumeratedPrintQueueTypes.Local, EnumeratedPrintQueueTypes.Connections]);

foreach (var queue in queues)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{queue.FullName}: IsOffline={queue.IsOffline}");

    var settings = new PrinterSettings
    {
        PrinterName = queue.FullName
    };

    // PrinterResolutions succeeds on the affected system.
    var resolutions = settings.PrinterResolutions;

    // For an offline queue this can terminate the process with 0xc0000005.
    var paperSize = settings.DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize;

    Console.WriteLine($"{paperSize.Width} x {paperSize.Height}");
}
```

The issue currently depends on the affected customer printer/driver configuration; a hardware-independent reproduction has not yet been produced.

### Expected behavior

The getter should return the paper size or throw a managed exception describing an invalid/unavailable printer or invalid driver data. It should not terminate the process.

### Actual behavior

Windows Application Error / .NET Runtime event:

```text
Application: FiftyWorker.exe
CoreCLR Version: 10.0.1226.42308
.NET Version: 10.0.12
Description: The process was terminated due to an unhandled exception.
Stack:
   at Windows.Win32.PInvoke.DocumentProperties(...)
   at Windows.Win32.PInvoke.DocumentProperties(...)
   at System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings.GetHdevmodeInternal(Char*)
   at System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings.GetHdevmode()
   at System.Drawing.Printing.PageSettings.get_PrinterResolution()
   at FiftyWorker.Local.GetPrinterList()
   at FiftyWorker.MainWindow..ctor()
   at FiftyWorker.Program.Main(System.String[])
```

A later property-isolation test identified `DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize` as the crashing read. Both `PageSettings.PaperSize` and `PageSettings.PrinterResolution` use the same `GetHdevmode()` path.

The corresponding Application Error entry was:

```text
Faulting module: coreclr.dll, version 10.0.1226.42308
Exception code: 0xc0000005
Fault offset: 0x00000000003596cf
```

### Workaround

Read `PrintQueue.IsOffline` before creating/querying `PrinterSettings`, and skip `DefaultPageSettings` for offline queues:

```csharp
if (queue.IsOffline)
{
    continue;
}

var settings = new PrinterSettings { PrinterName = queue.FullName };
var paperSize = settings.DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize;
```

### Similar issue search

No issue matching the offline-printer `0xc0000005` failure was found in `dotnet/winforms` using these searches:

- `DocumentProperties GetHdevmode`
- `DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize AccessViolation`
- `GetHdevmode crash`
- `printer offline access violation`

The closest result is #8812, which contains the same `PaperSize -> GetHdevmode -> DocumentProperties` stack but concerns missing `winspool.drv` on Windows Nano Server and is not a duplicate of this failure.

### Additional information still needed

- Exact Windows edition, version and OS build from the affected system.
- Affected printer queue type: local, shared/network connection, redirected, or other.
- Printer model, driver name, driver provider, driver version/date, INF name and port type. Queue/server/customer names may be anonymized.
- Whether the queue was already offline when the process started.
- Whether the failure remains after restarting the Print Spooler or recreating that exact queue.
- If safely obtainable outside production: a crash dump captured for the original failing build and analyzed with native symbols.
- Result with the latest supported .NET 10 servicing runtime, if newer than `10.0.12` is available when the report is submitted.
- Whether a minimal standalone x64 console/WPF application reproduces on the affected system.

## Safe collection commands for the affected machine

These commands only read system/spooler metadata. They do not query `DefaultPageSettings.PaperSize` and therefore do not intentionally execute the crashing code path.

```powershell
Get-ComputerInfo |
    Select-Object WindowsProductName, WindowsVersion, OsBuildNumber, OsArchitecture

dotnet --info
dotnet --list-runtimes

Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer |
    Select-Object Name, DriverName, PortName, Network, Shared, WorkOffline,
        PrinterStatus, DetectedErrorState

Get-CimInstance Win32_PrinterDriver |
    Select-Object Name, Version, InfName, DriverPath, SupportedPlatform
```

Review and anonymize printer names, server names, port names, user names and local paths before posting the output publicly.

Issues.Body: Fixes #15162 ## Root Cause This regression was most likely introduced by PR #13608. In the button rendering of DarkMode, the focus frame is changed to the ControlPaint.DrawFocusRectangle(...) path; under this color combination of .NET 11, black pixels will appear in the focus point line, resulting in a "black dot line" in the visual sense. ## Proposed changes - Added a shared `DrawDottedFocusRectangle(...)` method to `ButtonDarkModeRendererBase` that draws the focus rectangle using a specific dotted pen (eliminating reliance on the color-blending results of `ControlPaint.DrawFocusRectangle`). - Updated both `FlatButtonDarkModeRenderer` and `PopupButtonDarkModeRenderer` to use this shared method for rendering the focus indicator. - Added a regression test, `FlatButtonDarkModeRenderer_FocusIndicator_DoesNotPaintBlackPixels`, to ensure the dotted focus line no longer produces black pixels. ## Customer Impact - In Dark Mode, the focus indicator becomes clearly visible (a bright dashed line) when a button is focused via the Tab key, improving readability and accessibility; the change is limited to the rendering layer, with no changes to the public API. ## Regression? - Yes ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Test methodology - Manual ## Test environment(s) - 11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15196)

Issues.Title: Fix Issue 15190: TreeNodeCollection indexer setter throws NullReferenceException for a TreeNode not attached to a TreeView (regression since .NET 6)
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15190 

## Root Cause
This regression appears to have been introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/4297. Following changes in .NET 6, the indexer setter (`this[int index]`) for `TreeNodeCollection` introduced logic to prevent duplicate nodes; however, it assumes the owner is already bound to a `TreeView` and directly accesses `_owner._treeView!`.
When the owner is a detached `TreeNode` (not yet attached to any `TreeView`), `_owner._treeView` is `null`, triggering a `NullReferenceException` during subsequent access to `tv.Handle` or `tv._nodesByHandle`.

## Proposed changes

- Change the resolution of the setter's owner to a nullable-safe flow (using `TreeView? tv = _owner.TreeView`), handling both the detached and attached scenarios.
- For detached paths: Retain the legacy "managed-only" replacement semantics (to avoid NREs and support reordering via swap/sort); and add `_owner.CheckParentingCycle(value)` to prevent circular references.
- For the `attached` path: Retain existing cross-TreeView and duplicate-node protections; continue using the `Remove(actual)` + `Insert(index, value)` approach to ensure consistency in states such as handles, the node table, tooltips, and accessibility.

## Customer Impact

- Fixed a regression affecting .NET 6+: Swapping nodes via the indexer on a detached `TreeNodeCollection` for sorting purposes no longer throws a `NullReferenceException`.
- Restored behavior consistent with earlier versions (allowing nodes to be reordered while detached before being attached to a `TreeView`).
